The absorption line energy of \(3.9 \times 10^{-6}\,\text{eV}\) corresponds to a wavelength of about 31.8 cm. This is consistent with the 21 cm hydrogen line (rest energy \(\sim 5.9 \times 10^{-6}\,\text{eV}\)) redshifted by a factor of \(1+z \approx 1.5\) (\(z \approx 0.5\)), matching the source distance of 2.1 Gpc. The observed line is the redshifted 21 cm hyperfine transition of neutral atomic hydrogen (HI).

In the Milky Way, the 21 cm line is produced by atomic hydrogen. When seen in absorption against a bright background radio source, the line primarily traces the **cold atomic interstellar medium** (cold neutral medium, CNM), because the colder gas has a lower spin temperature and produces stronger, narrower absorption features. The warm atomic medium contributes more to emission.

**Answer: C**
